findings.description: Failure has no specified construction surface. architecture.contracts[4] defines accessors only (code/message/fix/retryable), but tk-0003 must emit InvalidArguments/UNI-ARGS-INVALID from clap rejections while tk-0002 must emit InvalidConfiguration and ConfigurationRead. The type is core-owned and sealed at wave 0, so neither wave-1 lane can add constructors without a frozen-signature reconciliation mid-flight. Smallest correction: name the public constructors in the baseline contract, e.g. Failure::invalid_configuration(Location), Failure::configuration_read(ReadFailure, Option<Location>), Failure::invalid_arguments(Option<&str>), and state that code/message/fix text is core-owned.
findings.evidence: impl-guide.dd.json#architecture/contracts[4] (core failures) and [9] (CLI response contract requiring kind invalid_arguments and code UNI-ARGS-INVALID); units tk-0001.paths owns crates/core/**; tk-0002 and tk-0003 fences exclude it.

findings.description: tk-0005 owns crates/testkit/fixtures/consumer/** and crates/testkit/fixtures/architecture/**, both of which must contain Cargo manifests (the architecture fixture declares a forbidden edge; the consumer fixture declares a path dependency on the SDK). A live nested Cargo.toml inside a workspace member's directory is a known Cargo failure mode, and the remedy lives in the root manifest, which is tk-0001-owned and frozen in baseline.files before tk-0005 starts. Smallest correction: add exclude = ["crates/testkit/fixtures/**"] to the baseline root-manifest contract now, or state in tk-0005.interface that fixture manifests ship as non-buildable templates materialised into the temporary root by unisphere-proof and unisphere-arch-check.
findings.evidence: impl-guide.dd.json#units/tk-0005/paths; #architecture/contracts[2] (root Cargo.toml declares only resolver/members/edition/version/workspace dependencies); #baseline/files includes Cargo.toml; #checks/vd-0005 and vd-000a depend on those fixtures.

findings.description: tk-0004's write fence omits Cargo.lock while tk-0004.interface and composition step 6 both require the PM to refresh it during composition. Cargo.lock appears in tk-0001.paths and, correctly, not in baseline.files; it is absent from tk-0004.paths. The composed commit therefore carries a lockfile write that no tk-0004 fence authorises, which a fence check at compose --import or --verify is designed to catch. Smallest correction: add Cargo.lock to tk-0004.paths and leave root Cargo.toml tk-0001-only so a new shared dependency stays an explicit baseline reconciliation.
findings.evidence: Verified mechanically: 'Cargo.lock' in units/tk-0001/paths = true, in units/tk-0004/paths = false, in baseline/files = false. impl-guide.dd.json#units/tk-0004/interface and #composition/steps[5].

findings.description: ac-0003's claim that library calls do not read ambient HOME, environment or global config has no executable negative proof; its only listed check is vd-0002, an in-process cargo test -p unisphere-sdk suite. That suite cannot host the hostile-ambient fixture bp-0003 requires: sealed_command builds a subprocess environment, tk-0002 ships no binary, and std::env::set_var is unsafe and not parallel-safe under edition 2024, which ac-0008 independently forbids. A FakeReader call-recorder proves no reader access, not no ambient access. ac-0008's no-network claim is likewise unasserted by vd-0002/0003/0004/000a. Smallest correction: add vd-000a to ac-0003's proof list and require unisphere-proof sdk-consumer to run the external consumer under sealed hostile HOME/XDG_*/UNISPHERE_* values asserting the resolved Configuration is unchanged; state the no-network property as a dependency-surface argument or drop it from the proven set.
findings.evidence: impl-guide.dd.json#capabilities/ac-0003/proof lists only vd-0002; #checks/vd-0002 args are ['test','-p','unisphere-sdk','--lib','--tests']; #architecture/contracts[10] scopes sealed_command to subprocess environments; backpressure.dd.json#rows/bp-0003 requires a hostile ambient HOME/env fixture.

findings.description: The declared toolchain pin is inert on the observed host. rust-toolchain.toml is a rustup mechanism; rustup is absent here, so the file is silently ignored, and on a rustup-equipped coder clone it instead forces a 1.95.0 download with components. Observed component versions are also incoherent with the declared channel, so vd-0008 and vd-0009 would execute under components from a different toolchain than the declared rustc, and ac-0009's documented toolchain would be a file rather than evidence. Smallest correction: keep rust-toolchain.toml but stop treating it as the pin; have tk-0005's checks extension record and assert observed rustc/cargo/clippy/rustfmt versions, and document the observed baseline in docs/development.md.
findings.evidence: Observed by --version probes only: rustc 1.95.0 (59807616e 2026-04-14) (Homebrew), cargo 1.95.0, rustfmt 1.9.0-stable (88d9e12ae1 2026-08-18), clippy 0.1.98 (88d9e12ae1 2026-08-18); 'command -v rustup' returned nothing. impl-guide.dd.json#architecture/contracts[13] declares channel 1.95.0 with rustfmt/clippy; #checks/vd-0008 and vd-0009.

findings.description: vd-0002's tests/service_in_isolation.rs technique requires #[path]-including src/service.rs into an integration-test crate, which compiles only if that module contains no crate:: or super:: references. The constraint is unstated and would surface as late rework in tk-0002. Smallest correction: one clause in tk-0002.interface requiring the isolated service module to be self-contained, referring to dependencies only through absolute unisphere_core:: and serde_json:: paths.
findings.evidence: impl-guide.dd.json#units/tk-0002/interface ('tests/service_in_isolation.rs compiles the actual service module without fs/wiring modules').

findings.description: No check executes the real binary's human render path. stdout_is_terminal is injected through CliContext so vd-0003 covers both branches in-process, but the actual terminal capture lives in tk-0004's crates/app/src/main.rs and vd-000b runs the installed binary with captured stdout, i.e. machine mode only. Smallest correction: have unisphere-proof installed-cli invoke the installed binary once with explicit --human and assert the human projection and stream routing, or record the terminal-detection limit explicitly against ac-0005.
findings.evidence: impl-guide.dd.json#architecture/contracts[8] (context captured only in main) and [9] (human success stdout, human failure stderr); #capabilities/ac-0005/proof lists vd-0003 and vd-0004; #checks/vd-000b.

findings.description: The claim that Node, OMP and Builder are unavailable at product runtime has no named mechanism. sealed_command is contracted as temporary HOME/config roots plus scrubbed relevant variables, with no mention of PATH, and tk-0005 is explicitly forbidden from modifying testkit's lib to add it. Smallest correction: name PATH reduction explicitly in the baseline sealed_command contract owned by tk-0001, before sealing.

findings.description: An oversize ConfigSource::Inline payload has no assigned failure kind. MAX_CONFIG_BYTES is contracted to apply to inline bytes as well as file reads, but ReadFailure::TooLarge maps to ConfigurationRead, which describes a read that never happened for inline input, and InvalidConfiguration is not stated either, while vd-0004 is told to exercise oversized fixtures. Smallest correction: state which kind and code an oversize inline payload produces.
findings.evidence: impl-guide.dd.json#architecture/contracts[5] (MAX_CONFIG_BYTES applies to inline bytes and file reads) and [4] (FailureKind and codes); #checks/vd-0004 description.
